title: Atlassian Patches 75 Flaws in Data Center and Server Products
description: Atlassian's October 2026 security bulletin addresses 75 unique vulnerabilities affecting its Data Center and Server products, including Bamboo, Bitbucket, Confluence, Crowd, Fisheye/Crucible, Jira Software, and Jira Service Management. Among these, 14 are critical-severity issues primarily in third-party components such as Apache Tomcat, Bouncy Castle, Netty, and Apache SSHD. Atlassian assesses the risk from these third-party component vulnerabilities as lower and non-critical for their products. The bulletin includes a variety of issues such as denial-of-service, cryptographic weaknesses, authentication and authorization problems, SSRF, information disclosure, and code execution bugs. Atlassian recommends updating to the latest product versions or fixed releases to mitigate these vulnerabilities. There is no indication of active exploitation in the wild for these issues.
aiSummary: Atlassian's October 2026 security bulletin lists 75 unique CVEs affecting multiple Data Center and Server products, with 14 critical-severity flaws all tied to third-party dependencies like Apache Tomcat, Bouncy Castle, Netty, and Apache SSHD. The affected products include Bamboo, Bitbucket, Confluence, Crowd, Fisheye/Crucible, Jira Software, and Jira Service Management. The critical vulnerabilities include CVE-2026-65637, CVE-2026-65182, CVE-2026-68525 (Apache Tomcat), CVE-2026-58062 (Bouncy Castle), CVE-2026-75595 (Netty), and CVE-2026-77185 (Apache SSHD). Atlassian notes that the use of these components presents a lower, non-critical risk to their customers. The bulletin also covers high-severity issues affecting widely used open source libraries, with vulnerability types ranging from denial-of-service to code execution. Atlassian urges customers to update to the latest versions or fixed releases and states no known exploitation in the wild for these vulnerabilities.
aiImpact: The vulnerabilities affect multiple Atlassian Data Center and Server products through third-party components, potentially exposing them to denial-of-service, cryptographic weaknesses, authentication and authorization issues, SSRF, information disclosure, and code execution risks. However, Atlassian assesses the risk to their customers as lower and non-critical due to their specific use of the affected components. No active exploitation has been reported. Failure to update could leave systems exposed to these issues.
